newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse to upgrade computer system in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse to upgrade computer system in 1997.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange plans to buy a computer system next year that will help it compete for capital with Western European bourses, the exchange's president said on Thursday.
"We want to be a competitor of other bourses, and probably in three or four years the Polish bourse will compete with bourses in Paris, Frankfurt and London," Wieslaw Rozlucki told reporters.
Rozlucki said the new client-server system would allow the linking of an unlimited number of terminals and also help ease the work of brokers.
He said he hoped the system, worth several million dollars, would be purchased in the second quarter next year and be entirely in place by the end of 1998.
